n, k = map(int, input().split())

mod = 10**9+7

class Matrix:
    def __init__(self, n=0, m=0):
        self.h = n
        self.w = m
        self.a = [0] * (n * m)

    def get(self, r, c):
        return self.a[r * self.w + c]

    def set(self, r, c, val):
        self.a[r * self.w + c] = val

    def __iadd__(self, m):
        assert self.h == m.h and self.w == m.w
        for i in range(self.h * self.w):
            self.a[i] += m.a[i]
        return self

    def __isub__(self, m):
        assert self.h == m.h and self.w == m.w
        for i in range(self.h * self.w):
            self.a[i] -= m.a[i]
        return self

    def __imul__(self, m):
        assert self.w == m.h
        ret = Matrix(self.h, m.w)
        for i in range(self.h):
            for j in range(m.w):
                s = 0
                for k in range(self.w):
                    s += self.get(i, k) * m.get(k, j)
                ret.set(i, j, s % mod)
        self.h, self.w, self.a = ret.h, ret.w, ret.a
        return self

    def __add__(self, m):
        res = Matrix(self.h, self.w)
        for i in range(self.h * self.w):
            res.a[i] = self.a[i] + m.a[i]
        return res

    def __sub__(self, m):
        res = Matrix(self.h, self.w)
        for i in range(self.h * self.w):
            res.a[i] = self.a[i] - m.a[i]
        return res

    def __mul__(self, m):
        res = Matrix(self.h, m.w)
        for i in range(self.h):
            for j in range(m.w):
                s = 0
                for k in range(self.w):
                    s += self.get(i, k) * m.get(k, j)
                res.set(i, j, s % mod)
        return res

def identity(n):
    ret = Matrix(n, n)
    for i in range(n):
        ret.set(i, i, 1)
    return ret

def power(a, n):
    assert a.h == a.w
    ret = identity(a.h)
    base = a
    while n:
        if n & 1:
            ret *= base
        base *= base
        n >>= 1
    return ret

# Initialize matrices
matrices = [Matrix(2 * k + 1, 2 * k + 1) for _ in range(65)]
for i in range(66):
    for j in range(i):
        matrices[i].set(0, j, 1)
    for j in range(2 * k):
        matrices[i].set(j + 1, j, 1)
    matrices[i].set(2 * k, 0, 1)
    matrices[i].set(2 * k, 2 * k, 1)

def compute(i, k):
    return power(matrices[i + k], k - i) * power(matrices[i], i)

def solve(n, k):
    count = 0
    tmp = n
    while tmp:
        tmp //= k
        count += 1
    b = [Matrix(2 * k + 1, 2 * k + 1) for _ in range(count + 5)]
    c = [Matrix(2 * k + 1, 2 * k + 1) for _ in range(count + 5)]
    d = [Matrix(2 * k + 1, 2 * k + 1) for _ in range(k + 1)]
    b[0] = matrices[k - 1]
    c[0] = power(b[0], k - 1)
    b[1] = compute(k - 1, k)
    c[1] = power(b[1], k - 1)
    s = identity(2 * k + 1)
    for j in range(2, count + 2):
        b[j] = compute(k - j % k, k)
        s *= c[j - 1]
        b[j] = b[j] * s
        c[j] = power(b[j], k - 1)
    idx = 1
    rem = n % k
    n -= rem
    q = 0
    tmp = n
    if tmp:
        while tmp % k == 0:
            q += 1
            tmp //= k
    q = (k - q % k) % k
    ans = identity(2 * k + 1)
    ans = power(matrices[q], rem) * power(matrices[q + k], max(rem - q, 0))
    n //= k
    if n == 0:
        return (ans.get(2 * k, 0) + ans.get(0, 0)) % mod
    n -= 1
    while n:
        t = n % k
        if t:
            ans *= power(b[idx], t)
        n //= k
        idx += 1
    ans *= b[1]
    return (ans.get(2 * k, 0) + ans.get(0, 0)) % mod

print(solve(n, k))
